solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Half of landed fish's heading here?

definitions.text: Half of landed fish's heading here?

indicators.note: taking half of a word means the back half is dropped and only the front half kept

parts.note: a landed fish has been caught

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, the one at its head

parts.note: the first letter of fish

explanation.surface: An angler asks whether this is where half of the day's catch is headed.
explanation.walkthrough: CAU is the first half of CAUGHT; add F. The whole clue also describes a CAUF, a perforated chest in which caught fish are kept alive in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauf is a floating perforated box for storing live fish after catching them, so it is literally where landed fish are kept.

clue.text: Coming back down with a cold melon

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the following string is read from its end

parts.note: French 'à bas', a cry meaning down with
taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Someone returning from a trip downstairs with a chill and a melon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down with' is one unit, the French slogan à bas; ABAS + A + C, all read backwards, gives CASABA.
explanation.definitionFit: A casaba is a variety of winter muskmelon with yellow rind and sweet pale flesh.

clue.text: Abounding with lumps, not tons

indicators.note: not here tells the solver to leave the named letter out of the word

parts.note: tuberous means having tubers or knobbly swellings
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Something lumpy and plentiful, though without any heavy weight to it.
explanation.walkthrough: TUBEROUS loses its T to give UBEROUS, a rare word related to udder and Latin uber, fruitful.
explanation.definitionFit: Uberous is an archaic adjective for fruitful, copious or plentiful, from Latin uber meaning rich or fertile.

clue.text: Turning in after case of fine spirit

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the two letters that enclose the rest

parts.note: the outside letters of fine

indicators.note: turning a short word around means reading it in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Heading in to bed after a glass of good liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is not a link here: it puts the turned word second.
explanation.definitionFit: Feni is a strong liquor distilled in Goa from cashew apples or coconut sap, so a type of spirit.

clue.text: Palace player overacting when beset by a large supporter

indicators.note: something beset by others is surrounded on all sides by them

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
a ham is an actor who overacts
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A hammy palace performer surrounded by a big-bodied backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but here it is an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex at Granada in southern Spain.

clue.text: AA gun that is put on border, mile away

indicators.note: away means gone, so the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches
M is the abbreviation for mile
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An anti-aircraft gun placed on a frontier some way off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put on' places the first part above the second. Archie was the airmen's nickname for flak.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie was First World War slang among airmen for anti-aircraft fire or an anti-aircraft gun.

clue.text: Wind damage to get island obliterated

parts.note: to harm is to damage

indicators.note: obliterated means wiped out, so that letter vanishes from the word

parts.note: to attain something is to get it
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A storm does so much damage that an island is wiped off the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The harmattan is a dry, dusty trade wind blowing from the Sahara across West Africa in winter.

clue.text: Voodoo priestess topped pulpit

indicators.note: topped means its top cut off, which in a down entry is the first letter

parts.note: a mambo is a voodoo priestess in Haiti

explanation.surface: A voodoo priestess has been ousted from the pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: MAMBO without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised stand or pulpit in early Christian churches, from which the readings were given.

clue.text: Playing airs with thumbs? These thus used

definitions.text: Playing airs with thumbs? These thus used

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are tossed about and set in a fresh order
used up means consumed, so the letters of that word are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Plucking tunes with one's thumbs: these instruments are played like that.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H, U, S from THUMBS to leave MB, then mix with AIRS. Read whole, the clue describes the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Mbiras are African thumb pianos, whose metal tongues are plucked with the thumbs to play tunes.

clue.text: E-tailer cut loose to distribute via network …

indicators.note: cut loose, the letters are freed from their order and can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An online seller breaks free to sell its goods through a network.
explanation.definitionFit: To reticulate is to divide or spread something, such as water or electricity, through a network of channels or pipes.

clue.text: … domain hosting a new group of web developers

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so this word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a domain is a field or area
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A website domain playing host to a fresh crowd of web designers.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N go inside AREA. The web developers are spiders, which develop webs, not websites.
explanation.definitionFit: Aranea is a genus of orb-weaving spiders, a group of creatures that build webs.

clue.text: Learner leaving one of two toddlers stifling a little gasp, reckless driver

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, holding it in the middle
the letter is leaving only one of the pair, so it drops out of the first copy

parts.note: a toddler walks slowly, so is an ambler; two of them side by side
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small part of it, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of gasp

explanation.surface: A learner driver steers off from two small children, who let out a little gasp at the reckless driving.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first of the pair loses its L; the gasp goes between the two words, which reads as one swallowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amber gambler is a motorist who speeds through traffic lights as they change from green to red, risking a crash.

clue.text: Pantry right for syrup?

parts.note: a spence is an old word for a larder or pantry
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A larder stocked with what is needed for making syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup here is a wig, from Cockney rhyming slang 'syrup of figs' for wig; the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer was an eighteenth-century kind of wig, and syrup is rhyming slang for a wig or toupee.

clue.text: Anarchic topical rag's a pain in the bum

indicators.note: anarchic means without order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chaotic satirical newspaper is a real annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for an irritation is meant literally: the answer is a medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Proctalgia is the medical name for pain in the rectum or anus, literally a pain in the backside.

clue.text: Flora/fauna of a region's lopped a small amount

indicators.note: lopped means cut off at the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: biota is the combined plant and animal life of an area

explanation.surface: A region's wildlife has been cut back to just a little.
explanation.walkthrough: BIOTA without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, is used to mean a tiny quantity, as in not one iota.

clue.text: Protein in edible shellfish, not one without spines

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second
not tells the solver to strike the named letters out of the word

parts.note: the abalone is an edible sea snail
taken as written, the letters to remove
actin is a protein found in muscle

explanation.surface: A protein found in shellfish you can eat, though not in one that lacks spines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' removes the word one itself, all three letters, rather than the digit I.
explanation.definitionFit: Abactinal describes the surface of a starfish or other radial animal away from the mouth and the rays, so lacking tube feet and spines.

clue.text: Girl with affinity for animal that's died accidentally

parts.note: mor is a dialect word for a girl
kin means related, of the same family or kind

explanation.surface: A girl with a gift for animals, mourning one that died by mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A morkin is an archaic term for a beast that has died by disease or accident, rather than being slaughtered.

clue.text: Kirkpatrick wanting to reserve excellent remote spot outside of Hamilton?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is missing from the word

parts.note: to book is to reserve
Ralph Kirkpatrick catalogued Scarlatti's sonatas, so they are numbered K
A1 means excellent, written with I for the 1

explanation.surface: Someone who failed to reserve a great out-of-the-way place beyond Hamilton.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOK without K, then AI. Hamilton is the New Zealand city, not the Scottish one; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Booai is New Zealand slang for remote back-country, as in 'up the booai', so somewhere far out from a city like Hamilton.

clue.text: Group of turtles surrounding can at sea hesitate

indicators.note: surrounding means going all around, so this word wraps the other

parts.note: bale is the collective noun for turtles

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: Turtles at sea circle a floating can and hesitate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the turtles so well it hides that it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance in an old intransitive sense means to waver or hesitate, weighing one choice against another.

clue.text: Bee perhaps cutting around meadow

indicators.note: around means encircling, so this word goes round the next

parts.note: acute means sharp, so cutting
a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: A bee buzzing around a meadow being mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a bee is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An aculeate is a stinging insect of the Hymenoptera, such as a bee, wasp or ant, from Latin for prickly.

clue.text: Is a leg broken with absolute sensitivity to pain?

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for absolute

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a broken leg is why the patient feels pain so keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Algesia is the medical term for capacity to feel pain, or heightened responsiveness to painful stimuli.

clue.text: Smell most of familiar reality

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: old means familiar, as in an old friend
a fact is a reality

explanation.surface: Most of what you know of the world comes through your nose.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD without its last letter, then FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfact is a rare verb meaning to smell, related to olfactory and the Latin for scenting.

clue.text: Private widow's rights kept back

indicators.note: kept back suggests going backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: in old Scots law a terce was a widow's right to a third of her husband's heritable estate

explanation.surface: A widow's legal entitlements are concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept back' looks like withholding, which suits the surface, but it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret and private are synonymous adjectives, both meaning kept from public knowledge.

clue.text: Really behave badly losing last friend

indicators.note: losing its last letter means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to act up is to misbehave
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone truly misbehaves after their latest friend walks away.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT UP without its last letter, then ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually and really are interchangeable adverbs meaning in fact or in truth.

clue.text: Slips perhaps and comes back to life?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwear, of which slips are an example
second meaning, read whimsically: reverses its death, un- plus dies

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and then revives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a made-up word: un-dies, undoing dying, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is informal for underwear, and a slip is a woman's undergarment, so slips are one example.

clue.text: Cried out sounding unproductive

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so a word is matched by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: yeld is a Scots word for barren, or a cow giving no milk

explanation.surface: Someone shouted, making no headway.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout loudly, so yelled is the past tense meaning shouted or called out.

clue.text: A cartel deployed cold-blooded beasts

indicators.note: deployed means sent out and arranged, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug cartel sent out its ruthless killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded' reads as ruthless gangsters, but it means literal reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerta is a genus of lizards, reptiles that are cold-blooded animals, the green lizards of Europe.

clue.text: Trifles regularly indulge one in Scotland

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of indulge
ae is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A Scot occasionally treats themselves to small luxuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugae is Latin for trivialities or jests, used in English for trifling things or minor writings.

clue.text: Cold in places on fine coverings of fledglings

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the earlier piece goes second

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the next

parts.note: loci is Latin for places
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: In fine weather, cold patches dotted on the downy coats of young birds.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside LOCI, and the result comes after F; in an across clue 'on' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Flocci are tufts of down, the soft fluffy covering of young birds before their true feathers grow.

clue.text: Scots urge accepting male god of love

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so this word holds the next one

parts.note: caa is a Scots verb to drive or urge on
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A Scotsman encourages a man to embrace the deity of love.
explanation.walkthrough: M inside CAA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cama, also spelt Kama, is the Hindu deity of desire and love, the counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Interminable hernia returning is concerning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the opposite way
interminable here means without its ends, so first and last letters go

parts.note: the middle of hernia, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hernia that keeps coming back is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' usually means endless in time; here it means having had its ends cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is a Latin phrase used in English meaning about or regarding, as in legal case titles.

clue.text: Jelly served in tea garden

indicators.note: served in means presented within the following words

parts.note: the end of tea joined to the start of garden

explanation.surface: Jelly was on offer at the tea garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a jelly for culture media and in cooking.

clue.text: Sean performing with Lambert in Highlander

indicators.note: performing means acting out, so the letters are put into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
L is the symbol for the lambert, a unit of brightness
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sean Connery acting alongside Christopher Lambert in the film Highlander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' seems to name the film but its two letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Nainsel, meaning own self, was used in literature for a Highland Scot, from the phrase 'her nainsel' put in Highlanders' mouths.

clue.text: … realism in films produced by creative men I fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are worked into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone imagines lifelike movies made by inventive directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinéma vérité is a documentary film style aiming at naturalism, using hand-held cameras and unscripted action.

clue.text: One teased with fruit demolished sultana after time

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the scrambled fruit follows the time piece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: A man who was tempted with fruit eventually devoured a sultana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' suggests eating, but it scrambles the letters. 'After time' puts T first.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Tantalus was punished in Hades with fruit and water that always moved just beyond his reach.

clue.text: Bury in Scotland? Oppose resolutely, no trace of belief in that

indicators.note: no means without, so the selected letter is taken away

parts.note: to beard someone is to confront them boldly

indicators.note: a trace is a tiny amount, so just the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of belief

explanation.surface: Laying someone to rest in Scotland, standing firm against all belief.
explanation.walkthrough: BEARD minus B. Bury is also a town in England, which the question mark plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eard is a Scots verb meaning to bury, related to the noun eard for earth or soil.
